newsitem.title: USA: US attache shaves India '96 soybean crop estimate.
newsitem.headline: US attache shaves India '96 soybean crop estimate.

text.p: A U.S. agricultural attache in New Dehli shaved his forecast for the 1996 India soybean crop to 3.8 million tonnes from 4.03 million tonnes, citing rising prices, reduced market arrivals and poor weather.
In a report dated Januar 31 that was released in Washington this week, the attache also said the Indian soybean processing industry was pushing for imports with "renewed vigor."

The attache estimated crush domestic consumption at 3.35 million tonnes, down from a previous estimate of 3.57 million tonnes and pegged total domestic consumption at 3.8 million tonnes, revised from 4.03 million tonnes seen earlier.

The attache said soybean prices are unusually high for this time of year and market arrivals have dropped. Larger farmers appear to be holding stocks of soybeans but less than ideal weather may have been more damaging to yields than initially estimated, the attache said.

The attache said the proposal to allow imports against re-exports of soybean meal has support from some government ministries but plant protection officials are concerned about disease and others worry about the impact on local growers.

"Nevertheless, the proposal to allow imports of soybeans and possibly other oilseeds has more momentum than it has had in the past, and could result in soybean imports if plant protection officials are persuaded to accept alternative certfication measures," the attache wrote in the report.
Attache reports are not official USDA data.
